points.description: States that the prototype program's role is to simulate (imitate/model) the behaviour of the desired software product, using the term 'simulate' or 'simulation' (or an exact equivalent such as 'imitate the behaviour').
points.partial_credit: Half marks if it says the prototype represents or models the software product but does not clearly say it simulates behaviour.

points.description: States that it simulates only portions/parts of the desired software product (a partial, not complete, version), not the whole system.

Correctly identifies what is simulated as the behaviour of the desired (final) software product, not just its appearance, code, or a finished product, and does not confuse the prototype with the final product or with a testing/debugging program.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the precise idea: a prototype simulates the behaviour of portions of the desired software product, with the word simulate (or exact equivalent) used. Part marks only when clearly more than half of a point is stated precisely. Vague statements (e.g. 'helps solve the problem', 'a test version') earn nothing, and wrong claims (e.g. that it is the final product) lose the affected point.
